# Fate UI v0.9.9-beta3

Angelcore gives Fate UI a terminal-style look while keeping the same sessions, files, Git tools, and browser. This beta also adds shareable skin folders and backgrounds made from your own images.

## A different look, not a different app

Angelcore is included with the app. Open **Settings → Skins** to try it; there is nothing extra to download. It replaces icon-heavy controls with text actions, gives the composer a command-style input, and lays out conversations as an open transcript. Your unfinished message stays put when you switch back to Default.

Color themes are separate from skins. Keep your current palette, or try the new Monochrome palette. The header lines, panel dividers, and plugin status spacing have also been cleaned up, including compact mode.

## Make a skin and share the folder

You can now import, preview, export, and remove skin packs from Settings. Imported folders live in `~/.pi/fateGUI/skins/`, alongside the rest of your Fate UI data, rather than inside the app installation.

Version 1 packs choose existing components and a small set of layout options. They can include a palette and a PNG background, but not JavaScript, CSS, or remote assets. Existing pack IDs are not silently overwritten, and missing or invalid packs fall back to Default.

The [Ashen Terminal example](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/tree/v0.9.9-beta3/examples/skins/ashen-terminal) is a starting point for trying imports or making your own pack. The [skin guide](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v0.9.9-beta3/docs/skins.md) covers the format and its limits.

## Bring your own background

Choose a local image in **Skins → Background**. Fate UI converts it into a still, dithered background behind the conversation and caches the result locally. You can adjust its strength or remove it. The image is not uploaded, and it is not reprocessed while you type or change colors.

The README now includes an Angelcore showcase captured from the actual app with demo content.

## Compatibility and downloads

Existing preferences and color themes are kept. Angelcore is optional; Default remains available.

Native installers are verified and smoke-tested on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64 before publication. Public beta installers are unsigned; verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS` and back up important work before upgrading.
